title: EIF at 25: Entergy, Ducks Unlimited help farmers improve wildlife habitat
summary: The project’s goals include increasing energy efficiency, converting ground water to surface water usage, improving water quality, optimizing irrigation water systems and providing wildlife habitat.
body_markdown:
NEW ORLEANS – Entergy is[celebrating](https://www.entergy.com/news/entergy-celebrates-25-years-of-local-sustainability-impact-through-environmental-initiative-fund) the 25th anniversary of its Environmental Initiatives Fund. During that time, Entergy shareholders have contributed nearly $45 million to community-based environmental projects across the region.


Entergy launched a[commemorative webpage](https://www.entergy.com/environment/eif) to mark this milestone. As part of the anniversary, Entergy is highlighting successful projects from across the region with profiles about local partners. The second part of the six-part series is below:


**Entergy, Ducks Unlimited help farmers improve wildlife habitat**


The Mississippi Alluvial Valley, historically known as the Mississippi Delta, is the largest contiguous floodplain and wetland ecosystem in North America. It covers roughly 24 million acres across seven states, including three in Entergy’s service territory: Arkansas, Mississippi and Louisiana.


In the nearly 10 million acres of irrigated cropland in the valley, water withdrawals in many areas exceed replacement rates. To address that concern and help farmers grow sustainable crops, in 2019, Entergy’s Environmental Initiatives Fund provided $250,000 to help Ducks Unlimited’s Rice Stewardship Partnership work with farmers, USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service and other agricultural producers in economically distressed areas of Arkansas, Louisiana and Mississippi to improve the sustainability of natural resources. The project’s goals include increasing energy efficiency, converting ground water to surface water usage, improving water quality, optimizing irrigation water systems and providing wildlife habitat. The project includes 200 farms on approximately 20,000 acres in the region.


“Our work with rice growers across Arkansas, Mississippi and Louisiana was a tremendous fit for Entergy’s Environmental Initiatives Fund because of the reduction in water use, greenhouse gas emissions and input costs for the farmers while improving water quality leaving the fields and providing habitat for waterfowl and other wildlife,” said Andi Cooper, director of foundation relations at Ducks Unlimited. “Today, the Rice Stewardship Partnership continues to deliver critical infrastructure and natural resource efficiencies across rice-growing states.”


In addition to EIF funding, Entergy offers an array of technical and financial assistance to rice producers within our service territory to improve farming efficiencies and environmental performance. Programs include electric line extensions to serve new irrigation wells, line extensions for diesel-to-electric pump conversions, automation of electric irrigation wells and special rate packages to help Entergy manage peak demand loads in summer.


“Entergy employees and customers depend on the same water, land, and food resources that Ducks Unlimited’s Rice Stewardship Partnership is working to sustain and improve, and many rice growers are also our customers,” said John Weiss, Entergy vice president of sustainability and environmental policy.


To read more success stories from Entergy’s Environmental Initiatives Fund, visit[Entergy.com/Environment/EIF](https://www.entergy.com/environment/eif) .
